chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reported to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Blessed is the person whom Allah sees weeping over a sin out of fear of Allah, when no one else has come to know of that sin.

key_terms.خَشْيَة: Khashyah - Fear/awe: a reverential fear of God that motivates righteous conduct and sincere repentance
key_terms.ذَنْب: Dhanb - Sin/transgression: an act of disobedience to God's commands
key_terms.طُوبَى: Tuba - Blessedness/blessed: a word denoting supreme happiness, also associated with a tree in Paradise

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the virtue of weeping privately over one's sins out of fear of Allah?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) declares blessedness for the person whom Allah observes weeping over a sin out of fear of Allah, when no one else knows about that sin. This hadith emphasizes private repentance and sincere contrition, teaching that the most genuine form of remorse occurs between a servant and God alone.
